description: Different tools allow different materials, thicknesses, coatings, and preparation steps, and staff keep having to restate the same exceptions when members bring in unsuitable materials. All spaces are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 30-year-old fabrication staff member fielding repeated material-compatibility questions
user_profile.context: Most members remember the basic rules, but the important exceptions are being rediscovered over and over
user_profile.communication_style: Rule-focused and practical, prefers compatibility rules tied to specific tool-material combinations

fact_sheet.fact: The SpectraLase 9000 can cut PlexiGlow Cast Acrylic up to a maximum thickness of 12mm.
Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) is strictly forbidden on the SpectraLase 9000 due to the release of toxic chlorine gas when cut.
The cutting bed size of the SpectraLase 9000 is 900mm x 600mm.
Wood materials for the SpectraLase 9000 must be uncoated and free of resin-based glues, with the exception of approved Baltic Birch Plywood.
Reflective materials, including mirrored acrylic and polished metals, cannot be processed on the SpectraLase 9000.
Anodized aluminum can be engraved on the SpectraLase 9000, but it cannot be cut.
The OmniForm 3X exclusively uses the makerspace-provided 1.75mm EcoPLA Filament.
Members are not permitted to bring their own filament for use in the OmniForm 3X.
The maximum build volume for the OmniForm 3X is 250mm x 210mm x 210mm.
ABS, PETG, and Nylon filaments are not compatible with the OmniForm 3X due to workshop ventilation limitations.
All 3D print jobs for the OmniForm 3X must be sliced using the 'Forge Standard' profile in the MakerNet Portal.
The Raptor CNC Mill can process 6061-T6 Aluminum up to a thickness of 50mm.
All personal materials for the Raptor CNC Mill must be inspected and approved by Tool Manager, Maria Rodriguez, before use.
Ferrous metals, such as steel or iron, are prohibited on the Raptor CNC Mill to prevent excessive wear on the spindle.
The standard end mill provided for general use on the Raptor CNC Mill is a 1/4 inch, 2-flute carbide bit.
The AquaCut 55 can cut materials, including hardened steel and granite, up to 100mm thick.
Tempered glass is forbidden on the AquaCut 55 as it will shatter into small, hazardous fragments under pressure.
The abrasive used in the AquaCut 55 is 80-grit garnet, which is supplied by the makerspace at the workstation.
Laminated materials like carbon fiber composites are prohibited on the AquaCut 55 due to the risk of delamination.
All non-standard materials require a Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) to be submitted for review via the MakerNet Portal at least 48 hours before the scheduled work time.
A material quarantine shelf for unapproved items is located next to Workstation B-7.
Forge & Fiber Collective sells pre-approved 300mm x 600mm sheets of 3mm Baltic Birch Plywood for $8 per sheet.
Scrap materials must be sorted into the designated bins labeled 'Wood,' 'Acrylic,' or 'Metal' located by the exit.
Safety glasses are mandatory at all times in the main workshop area, which is demarcated by a solid yellow line on the floor.
In case of a tool malfunction, press the nearest red emergency stop button and immediately contact Safety Officer Alex Chen at extension 555.
The Class ABC fire extinguisher for electrical and combustible fires is located to the right of the main workshop entrance door.
Users must complete the 'CNC-101 Safety Certification' course before operating the Raptor CNC Mill.
Approved PlexiGlow Cast Acrylic can be purchased from 'Anvilton Plastics' at 240 Industrial Drive.
Members receive a 10% discount at 'MetalWorks Depot' on all 6061-T6 Aluminum stock by showing their Forge & Fiber membership card.
Maria Rodriguez, the Tool Manager, is available for material consultations on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM at her desk.
Safety Officer Alex Chen's office is located at A-01, and he can be reached for non-emergencies by emailing achen@forgeandfiber.mock.

user_needs.description: A member brought PlexiGlow Cast Acrylic. What's the maximum cutting thickness for it on the SpectraLase 9000?
The same member wants to know if they can use mirrored acrylic. What's the rule on reflective materials for the laser cutter?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After asking about one type of acrylic, the user may ask about another variant, especially a tricky one like mirrored acrylic.

user_needs.description: A different member has some plywood. What are the specific restrictions on wood materials for the laser cutter?
What is the cutting bed size of the SpectraLase 9000 for laying out an approved PlexiGlow Cast Acrylic sheet?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After confirming the thickness limit for an allowed acrylic, a natural follow-up is whether the sheet will fit within the laser cutter's work area.

user_needs.description: What is the rule regarding Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) on the SpectraLase 9000?

Which common filament types like ABS or PETG are not compatible with the OmniForm 3X?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Once a user knows they can't use their own filament, they will likely ask about the compatibility of other common types they might be familiar with.

user_needs.description: What is the rule on using ferrous metals like steel on the Raptor CNC Mill?
